The public `predict(pdat, idat=None, batch_size=128)` function accepts two pandas DataFrames. Column names and categorical values are case-sensitive.

## `pdat`: application-level data

Each row describes one field application. `id`, `tan_app`, and `app_method` are required. Each `id` should identify exactly one row. Other variables are completed with the defaults below.

| Column | Description | Default |
|---|---|---:|
| `id` | Unique application identifier | Required |
| `tan_app` | Total ammoniacal nitrogen applied; kg/ha as N | Required |
| `app_method` | Application method | Required |
| `incorp` | Incorporation class | `none` |
| `time_incorp` | Delay to incorporation; h | `NA` if `incorp = "none"`; `0.05` otherwise |
| `till` | Tillage within the preceding seven days | `no` |
| `fer_origin` | Fertiliser origin | `cat` |
| `fer_form` | Fertiliser physical form | `liquid` |
| `fer_trt1` | Primary fertiliser treatment | `none` |
| `fer_trt2` | Secondary fertiliser treatment | `none` |
| `crop` | Crop present in the field | `grass` |
| `crop_z` | Crop height; cm | `10`; missing if `crop = bare soil` |
| `soil_type` | Soil class | `clay` |
| `app_rate` | Application rate; t/ha or m³/ha | Linear estimate from `tan_app` |
| `fer_dm` | Fertiliser dry matter; % | `6.59` |
| `fer_ph` | Fertiliser pH | `7.30` |
| `furrow_z` | Furrow depth; cm | Missing |
| `soil_water` | Volumetric soil water content | `0.27` |
| `soil_ph` | Soil pH | `6.5` |
| `soil_dens` | Soil density; g/cm³ | `1.14` |
| `soil_oc` | Soil organic carbon; % | `3.49` |

When `app_rate` is missing, the current parameters estimate it as:

`app_rate = 20.46 + 0.25 × tan_app`.

An omitted optional column and an explicit missing value receive the same default. 

Note that some predictors are interdependent. For example, `fer_form` and `fer_dm` should be considered together. A combination such as `fer_form = "solid"` and `fer_dm = 5` would be inconsistent.

## Accepted categorical values

- `app_method`: `bc` (broadcast), `bsth` (band spreading with trailing hose), `ts` (trailing
  shoe), `os` (open slot), `cs` (closed slot)
- `incorp`: `none`, `deep`, `shallow`
- `till`: `no`, `yes`, `unknown`
- `fer_origin`: `pig`, `cat`, `mix`
- `fer_form`: `liquid`, `solid`
- `fer_trt1`: `none`, `Anaerobic digestion`, `Diluted`, `Acidification`,
  `Irrigated`
- `fer_trt2`: `none`, `Separation`
- `crop`: `stubble`, `grass`, `cereal`, `maize`, `bare soil`
- `soil_type`: `clay`, `sand`, `sandy.loam`, `peat`, `loam`,
  `loamy.sand`, `sandy.clay.loam`, `silty.clay.loam`, `silty.loam`,
  `clay.loam`, `Calcaric Regosol`, `Haplic Luvisol`, `unknown`

Note that `fer_origin = "mix"` should only be used with anaerobic digestion (`fer_trt1 = "Anaerobic digestion"`). Unknown values raise a `ValueError`.

## `idat`: time-dependent data

`idat` is optional. Each row represents one time interval for one application. Each interval extends from the `ct` value of the previous row to the `ct` value of the current row. For the first row, the interval starts at 0, corresponding to the time of fertiliser application. Rows for each application must be supplied in increasing `ct` order.

| Column | Description | Behaviour when omitted |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | Application identifier linked to `pdat` | Required with `idat` |
| `ct` | Cumulative time since application; h | Required with `idat` |
| `air_temp` | Mean air temperature over the interval; °C | Default daily profile interpolated at `ct` |
| `wind_2m` | Mean wind speed at 2 m over the interval; m/s | Default daily profile interpolated at `ct` |
| `rain_rate` | Mean rainfall intensity over the interval | `0` |

When `idat` is omitted, the package uses `ct = 2, 4`, then 4-h intervals from 4 to 48 h, and 12-h intervals from 48 to 240 h. It assumes that `ct = 2` corresponds to 10 AM. The default temperature and wind speed profiles have daily means of 15 °C and 3 m/s, amplitudes of 5 °C and 1.2 m/s, respectively, and reach their maxima around 3 PM. Default rainfall is zero.

## Returned columns and model response

The returned data frame contains the completed inputs and two prediction columns. 

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `prediction_erel` | Predicted cumulative emission as a fraction of applied TAN (dimensionless) |
| `prediction_ecum` | Predicted cumulative emission (kg N-NH3/ha), calculated as `prediction_erel × tan_app` |

## Current training domain

The model was trained on 2,128 emission dynamics curves, representing 51,499 measurements obtained using different measurement methods: micrometeorological methods, cumulative passive samplers (cps), wind tunnels, and dynamic chambers. The figures below show the distributions of the variables in the training data.

These ranges describe marginal training distributions and do not imply that every combination of predictors is represented. In the following, P*x* denotes the *x*th percentile. Predictions involving strong extrapolation should therefore be interpreted cautiously.

### Time sequences and weather

Training trajectories have a median of 9 time points. The first observation is at or before 5 h for 95% of trajectories. Approximately 76% trajectories reach 72 h, 41% reach 120 h, 17% reach 168 h, and 1% reach 238 h.

Custom sequences should begin soon after application and retain enough time points to describe changing weather and management conditions. Avoid encoding a long horizon with only one or two widely separated observations.

| Weather variable | P5--P95 | P1--P99 |
|---|---:|---:|
| `air_temp` | 1.40--22.04 | -1.20--27.70 |
| `wind_2m` | 0.33--5.25 | 0.10--7.50 |

About 97.4% of training rows have `rain_rate = 0`. Among positive values, the median is 0.092, P95 is 1.789, and P99 is 2.828.

| `soil_ph` | 1,518 (71.3%) | 5.16--7.70 | 4.60--8.15 |

All four numerical soil variables were available simultaneously for 514 applications. Missing soil inputs were common in the training data.

| Crop | Training applications |
|---|---:|
| `grass` | 991 |
| `cereal` | 360 |
| `unknown` | 287 |
| `bare soil` | 225 |
| `stubble` | 187 |
| `maize` | 60 |
| `other` | 16 |
| `rapeseed` | 2 |

`crop_z` is available for 1,412 applications. Its marginal P5--P95 range is 5--28 cm and P1--P99 is 3--60 cm. Crop height is not applicable to bare soil; a positive height supplied with `crop = "bare soil"` raises an error.

### Fertiliser characteristics

The training data contain 1,028 cattle, 660 pig, 16 mink, 333 mixed, 78 other, and 13 mineral concentrate applications. The `other` and `mineral concentrate` categories are not exposed through the public API. The dataset includes 2,100 liquid and 26 solid products, as well as 2 products with an unknown form.

| Variable | Available applications | P5--P95 | P1--P99 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `fer_dm` | 2,126 (99.9%) | 1.57--9.48% | 1.08--17.24% |
| `fer_ph` | 1,986 (93.3%) | 6.50--8.20 | 5.61--8.50 |

| First treatment | Training applications |
|---|---:|
| `none` | 1,355 |
| `Anaerobic digestion` | 484 |
| `Acidification` | 105 |
| `Diluted` | 30 |
| `Irrigated` | 5 |

| Second treatment | Training applications |
|---|---:|
| `none` | 2,031 |
| `Separation` | 68 |

These tables report only treatment values accepted by the public API. The remaining applications use internal treatment categories that cannot be provided to `predict`.

### Management and application conditions

| Application method | Training applications |
|---|---:|
| `bsth` (band spreading with trailing hoses) | 876 |
| `bc` (broadcast) | 673 |
| `ts` (trailing shoe) | 301 |
| `os` (open slot) | 200 |
| `cs` (closed slot) | 75 |
| `pi` (pressurised injection) | 3 |

Only 55 applications report recent tillage (`till = "yes"`), while 1,810 report `no` and 263 use the `unknown` category.

Furrow depth is available for 84 applications, with a median of 20 cm and an observed range of 1.5--20 cm. It should be supplied only when relevant to the application method.

Most applications have no incorporation (2,063), compared with 58 shallow and 7 deep incorporations. Among incorporated applications, the median incorporation delay is 0.05 h. Long delays and deep incorporation are weakly represented.

| Variable | P5--P95 | P1--P99 |
|---|---:|---:|
| `tan_app` | 25.5--147.6 | 14.9--215.3 |
| `app_rate` | 14.3--100.0 | 9.6--133.3 |

Across the 2,128 training applications, `tan_app` and `app_rate` have a Pearson correlation of 0.47.
